intros.opening_hook: A strong opener shows its first visible change by frame 2-6 at 60 fps, or after one deliberate empty beat of 20-26 f that turns the first event into a hard cut; it never fades up from black or starts on a title card. The hook becomes readable information within about 40-70 f (a metric settled at 41 f, a seven-word line done at about 70 f), then passes its energy on by cutting at peak speed: E.in into the cut, with the next shot starting at that velocity. Brand is either held back (a number or a question first, the mark at most a corner tag until about 60% of the runtime) or shown as the mark alone, already moving; the full lockup is saved for the end. The sound for the first ~2 s stays sparse, about 14 dB under the body with no sub, and the drop lands on the first hard cut: kick on the cut frame, sub 8-12 f before it. Readable type moves at no more than 20 px/f (letters travel faded and resolve as the move slows), edges move at no more than 60-80 px/f with master motion blur above 12 px/f, and every hold stays alive with a 0.3-0.5 px/f drift or a 0.04-0.07 %/f breath.
intros.transition: A transition is a designed handoff, not a cut between unrelated pictures. Something always crosses the seam: a velocity, a shape held within ±20-30 px of the same screen point, a dot, a line or a stage colour. The default that carries most edits is the velocity handoff. The outgoing move speeds up about ×1.13-1.2 per frame over its last 16-24 f, the cut lands on its fastest frame at 25-40 px/f, and the incoming shot opens at that speed or faster and slows about ×0.92-0.94 per frame to rest in 45-90 f. A scale jump of 1.3-2.5x (8-9x for a frame-filling macro of a related mark) is invisible when the scale velocity matches in log space, about −8% per frame on both sides of the cut. One-take seams (morphs, irises, portals, carets) run 20-90 f and keep every element edge under about 80 px/f, and only flat mask edges may move faster. Polarity flips, where mean luma jumps by 150 or more of 255, are the loudest punctuation: put them on downbeats, once or twice per film. Blending appears only as 1-2 ghost frames at a motion peak, never as a crossfade seam.
intros.camera: The camera is one transform on one world container (src/lib/camera.ts). A shot frames a world point at a screen point at scale k, and lc() blends shots with k in log space, so a zoom keeps an even perceived speed and the subject travels a straight line. What makes camera work feel expensive is the speed profile more than the path. Moves arrive fast and brake (E.out, E.cam), cruise at 3 px/f or less under readable copy, and leave by accelerating over the last 18-24 f into a cut on the fastest frame, ending at 13-47 px/f, and the incoming shot is already moving when it opens. Hero moves are 2-3x pushes over 60-67 f on E.smooth, peaking around 4-5% scale per frame, with the caption starting in the last 25% of the move so the text and the settle land together. No hold is ever dead: a 0.04-0.07%/f creep or a 0.3-1.5 px/f drift runs under every read longer than about 30 f. Keep camera speed under 60-80 px/f at the frame edge, render anything above 12 px/f with the motion-blur pass (--blur), keep roll under 11 deg and give each act one rotation axis.
intros.typography_motion: Measured type arrives on expo-out moves that cover 30-45% of their travel on the first frame and settle in 12-24 f at 60 fps, staggered 4-10 f per word (20-24 f for a calm one-word-per-beat read). What matters most is the readable moment: a word is either legible from its first frame (40% strength, rising at most 0.6 em at about 14 px/f) or it flies faded and streaked and resolves only once it slows below 20 px/f, and it always lands sharp, with any blur gone by 60% of the move. Colour carries recency: the newest glyph or word arrives in the one accent and relaxes to ink over 12-24 f. Lines never freeze and never jump: layouts are pre-solved or re-centred on a critically damped spring, a landed line tightens 2-3% or drifts 0.3-0.5 px/f, and a hold swells about 6% on an ease-in into the cut. Typing is time-boxed (any length done in about 68 f, half of it visible within 6 f), and the film's one discrete trick (a step edit, a scramble, a letter morph) acts out the copy instead of decorating it.
intros.ui_choreography: UI choreography is layout logic in motion: every rect is a function of the frame and the product's state, siblings reflow from computed positions instead of crossfading, and a container is on screen before its contents, which start once their slot is about 60% open. Entrances decay with no overshoot (a 200 px window rise on E.out covers about half its travel in the first 6 f and settles in 50 f) and exits accelerate, handing over to the next panel or the cut on their fastest frame with at most a 4 f gap. Size every move from peak speed = distance x the token's peak slope / frames (E.out 6.2 on its first frame, E.inOut 7.7, E.contact 4.4 on its last, E.whip 3.8, E.rest 3.5, E.glide 3.0, E.smooth 2.9, E.ui 2.7, E.dolly 1.5), so UI text stays at or under 20 px/f and nothing passes about 70 px/f; scale spawns and collapses with lmix so a small surface does not explode on its first frame. Cadence carries meaning: 4-6 f per row reads as data streaming in, 5 f per dealt card as tactile, a 14 f metronome of inserts as abundance, and uneven gaps such as 4, 15 and 18 f as a person deciding. The strongest moves make one motion do two jobs, an incoming panel's edge pushing its neighbour or a hero holding its exact screen position while the world changes around it, so the edit happens inside the product instead of at a cut.
intros.data_and_numbers: Numbers are proof, so they must read at a glance and stay true on any paused frame: tabular figures, a fixed digit count, and every shown value computed from fd(frame) so no motion-blur sub-sample shows two values. Hero counts are short, 28-46 f, starting from a credible 85-90% of the target on a quad-out (E.type) so the last unit lands in the final ~6 f instead of stalling; ambient UI counters may run 36-104 f. Charts draw in 24-96 f, bars grow 12-20 f each at 1.6-5 f staggers with any group landing within 30 f, and every bar tip, scan edge or line head stays at or under about 60-70 px/f at 1080p. A figure starts changing on the frame its cause lands (a press, a landing, a tab; effects follow the interaction by 2 f) and then holds at least 36 f plus 6 f per word of its label under a 2-3% breath. The one accent marks the hero series or the chosen item while comparison data stays grey, and two numbers are never crossfaded in place: cut them, count them or roll them.
intros.product_demo: A product shot depends on cause and effect: every action has a visible cause, the state changes on the cause frame itself (a 1 f swap, never a crossfade), and the result holds at least 36 f before the camera leaves. Give small UI hero weight through scale contrast, not length: alternate a wide with a 2-5x macro of the exact control, or open on the value moment at 1.6-2.2x and pull back to context over about 56 f, landing the next UI event within 2 f of the settle. Product arrivals are real motion. A device or window enters already moving (about 20 px/f on its first frame, settled by 44 f on E.out), and scrolls, sheets and widening bars peak at 35-60 px/f under the motion-blur pass. Holds stay alive with a 2-4% breath push instead of a dead lock. A person types at 30 cps. A fast product types at 50-72 cps, or to a fixed 68 f time box, with the newest characters arriving in the accent. Wherever possible let the product's own behaviour do the editing (a headline that grows into the input bar, an element that stays put while the page rebuilds around it, a window that recedes to its corner), so every transition also shows a feature.
intros.logo_and_end_card: The end card is the film's poster. The lockup appears once, sized at 28-45% of frame width, resolves within about 36-80 f, then holds 90-120 f (1.5-2.0 s, never past ~150 f) while it keeps building: a 10-20% push on E.dolly and tracking that tightens 0.03-0.06 em over ~46 f. Anything static past 48 f reads as a stalled player. The strongest endings come out of the story instead of starting a new logo animation: the last object lands on the mark's exact position and size, or the product clears the stage to uncover it, or the opening's mechanic returns carrying the name. Scale moves run in log space (lmix). Collapses from 9-12x settle in 36-66 f, and the fastest frames are flat fill, low contrast or motion-blurred. The name follows the mark at 55-60% of its slide, with letters 2-3.5 f apart and readable type never faster than 20 px/f. Sound carries half the weight: cut the music dead on the end-card frame, leave ~36 f of near-silence, put one hit on the frame the name resolves, and let its tail decay to digital zero inside a tail of at least 60 f. The last frame must show the mark plus the name, with at most one CTA at 44-56 px that stays readable for at least 1.7 s, and it never fades to black.
intros.color_and_light: Colour carries meaning, so ration it. Keep one accent with one job. It should cover roughly 0.05-6% of frame pixels on average (peaking near 12%) on a stage that fills 85-90% of the frame, and it should change on cut or impact frames, never through slow fades. Brightness is the strongest lever here: give every shot a planned mean luma, spend polarity flips of 160-240 levels on downbeats and act changes, and use at most one inverted card (about 60 f) in a dark film. Light moves are short and asymmetric: accent floods rise in 10-12 f and release over 20-26 f, sheens cross in about 36 f, and washes rise over about 40 f and recede over about 90 f. Stages never freeze: breathe them ±15% luma on a period of about 160 f, or drift them under 1 px/f. Build every gradient from tonal steps of one hue mixed in OKLab with mixColor, on normal blend, and let a hard edge or a one-frame white flash do the work a glow would.
intros.texture_and_finish: Texture and finish decide whether a film built from code reads as photographed or as a slideshow, and almost all of it works at the edge of perception: grain at a sigma of 1-2 code levels (a 1.5-2% layer), dot fields about 4% off their ground, photo plates graded to 5-8% mean luma, gobo shadows drifting under 0.5 px/f. Speed is finished in the render, not faked per layer: anything over 12 px/f gets the 240-degree float-accumulated blur pass, holds sit under 2 px/f so they render pin-sharp, and no element passes about 70-80 px/f. Every soft ramp ships as a dithered PNG, because a CSS gradient spanning fewer than about 30 code values bands, and every texture that animates is keyed to fd(frame) so the motion-blur sub-samples agree. Each texture must name its job (context, material, concealment, a hit) and keep one strength for the whole film. One signature surface move (a 34 f scanline transmutation, a ring field, a locked mosaic) is plenty for a film.
intros.layout_and_composition: In motion, layout means two things: where the eye lands, and how space gets made when something new arrives. The default is one subject per frame. That is a UI card at 72-92% of frame width or one line of type no wider than 80%, with captured UI shown at about 2x so body text is at least 27 px at 1080p, and everything that is not the hero dimmed to 0.6-0.7 brightness or defocused. When something enters, the layout makes room physically rather than overlaying it: neighbours move 0.43x the newcomer's travel and start up to 28 f early, and centred lines re-centre on a critically damped spring (20-45 px over 16-38 f) and then keep a 0.4-1.5 px/f drift so type never freezes. Captions go in the space the subject leaves: a 25-30% band, at most 24% of the frame width, inset 8-10% from the edge, starting in the last 25% of the move. To show breadth, use flush cells with no gutters on one shared stage, looping on coprime periods so a change lands somewhere about every 20 f. Any mark inside a sentence sits on the baseline at cap height, in a reserved slot.
intros.pacing_structure: Pacing is the shape of speed over time, and the strongest films control it at three scales. Per shot the shape is a U: arrive on E.out over 20-50 f, keep living through the hold at 0.3-1 px/f (no near-dead run longer than about 22 f), then accelerate over the last 18-24 f so the cut lands on the fastest frame at 17-38 px/f and the next shot opens already moving. Stillness is spent like money. One near-still hold of 60-90 f on the key claim, or a 12-15 f freeze on true silence before the lockup, reads as intent only because everything else moves. Per sequence, repetition teaches the viewer: a fixed 180 f ask beat with answers of varying length, a second instance at 0.6x length, phrase chunks landing one per beat. Per film, acts sit on the bar grid (a 30-60 s launch splits roughly 19/14/58/9%), stage polarity flips 3-5 times, and the score's arrangement follows the acts, with 12-24 f music holes before key statements and every slam within ±1 f of a picture event.
intros.micro_interaction: A micro-interaction is the visible cause of a cut. The response starts on the press frame, never a beat later, and the result holds at least 36 f before the camera moves on. A press works as a light envelope, not a bounce: an accelerating attack of 8-12 f, a one-frame peak and a release about twice as long (tau about 8 f), with no scale overshoot, because spring overshoot is kept for true landings. Small elements get weight by deforming with speed. A tab pill whose leading edge arrives in 12 f and trailing edge in 20 f stretches to about 1.9x its width mid-travel, and a moving dot stretches to its rest length plus about 4-5 f of travel. A cursor arrives 6-12 f before it acts and the target shows its hover state about 4 f after arrival; the press goes down in 4 f and recoils in 8 f, with at most one click per 30 f at uneven gaps such as 4, 15 and 18 f. Keep sound sparse: about 6-8 dry ticks in 45 s, each on the frame its element reaches 50% opacity and 12-18 dB under the landing hit, stepping up about 3 dB per action only across a counted run.
intros.depth_and_3d: Depth looks expensive only when it is physical and used sparingly. Use one rotation axis per act and perspective of 1800-2600 px for UI planes (about 3-4x the object's width for a small icon or coin), and tilt live components that have their own shadow and ground, never tilted screenshots. Most moves here are short and offset, not simultaneous: flips run 10-12 f, a tilt resolves over 20 f starting 6 f before the position settles, an unfold takes 24 f, and the state change lands on the edge-on or peak-tilt frame. Long moves (de-skews of 81 f, dollies of 60-68 f) ride E.cam or E.rest so they start gently and settle slowly. Keep speed honest: E.out puts about 5.5x its mean speed into the first frame (E.in into the last), so cap travel to keep peaks near 70 px/f and let the master's sub-frame blur carry anything over 12 px/f. Chromium decides the finish: keep roll outside the tilt and at most 11 deg, sort layers by z yourself (overflow, opacity and filters flatten preserve-3d), lay text out at shot scale with CSS zoom, and rack depth of field with RackFocus copies, never an animated filter blur.
